jobs.occupation: Scientist – Federated Accounting Framework & Service Architecture for the Accounting4NFDI Project (Physiker/in)
jobs.description: For our location in Hamburg we are seeking:Scientist – Federated Accounting Framework & Service Architecture for the Accounting4NFDI ProjectLimited: 2 years | Start: 01.02.2027 | ID: FHMA026/2026 | Deadline: 18.11.2026 | Full-time/Part-time | Remote work possibleDESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. Its research focuses on decoding the structure and function of matter, from the smallest particles of the universe to the building blocks of life. In this way, DESY contributes to solving the major questions and urgent challenges facing science, society and industry. With its ultramodern research infrastructure, its interdisciplinary research platforms and its international networks, DESY offers a highly attractive working environment in the fields of science, technology and administration as well as for the education of highly qualified young scientists.Distributed research infrastructures (compute, storage, licenses, facilities, scientific instruments and digital services) require transparent usage information to support sustainable operation and fair access. Accounting4NFDI is developing a unified, federated accounting framework for NFDI consortia and services. Based on FAIR principles, the framework will align with EOSC requirements and is intended to become a Base4NFDI service that interoperates with existing infrastructures rather than replacing them. DESY and the University of Freiburg jointly lead the work package "Accounting Framework, Service Concept and Dashboard". At DESY, you will conduct independent scientific and conceptual work on the accounting model, federated service and interface architecture, reporting and dashboard concepts, and their validation across heterogeneous research infrastructures. Your focus will be on developing, evaluating and generalising models and architectural concepts for interoperable research infrastructures.About your role:- Scientifically analyse and abstract hetero­geneous accounting requirements of research infrastructures and develop a unified, resource-oriented accounting and information model- Develop and evaluate a federated service, integration and information architecture for Accounting4NFDI, including concepts and specifications for interoperable APIs and exchange formats- Develop reporting and dashboard concepts based on the accounting framework, including suitable attributes, aggregations and evaluation logic for different stakeholder groups- Methodically validate accounting models, architecture and interface concepts through use cases, Proofs of Concept (PoCs) and integration scenarios, and derive generalisable findings for further development- Document, publish and present scientific and technical results; contribute to workshops, knowledge transfer and community engagement within NFDI, Base4NFDI and EOSCAbout you:- Completed University degree in Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics or a comparable field, a PhD or equivalent experiences is helpful- Strong knowledge of data/information modelling, federated architectures, web APIs and interoperable exchange formats- Fluent German and English (project language)- Excellent analytical and conceptual skills; able to work independently on scientific/technical questions- Experience in interdisciplinary collaboration and documenting complex concepts- Strong communication and presentation skills; able to discuss and defend concepts across stakeholder groups- Familiarity with FAIR principles, Open Science and research infrastructures- Knowledge of NFDI, Base4NFDI and/or EOSC- Knowledge of OAuth2/OIDC and IAM4NFDI- Advantage: experience with reporting/dashboards or data harvesting/aggregationGood reasons to join:Look forward to a unique working environment on our international research campus. Respectful cooperation and the well-being of our staff are central to us, with gender equality forming a key part of this commitment. To support work life balance we offer flexible working hours, variable part-time, job-sharing models and participation in mobile work (up to 50 %). You will benefit from our family-friendly and collegial atmosphere, our established health management and occupational pension provision. As a public funded employer, we offer you a secure workplace and facilitate your individual career with our comprehensive training and development opportunities. jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher positions - Statistical Physics and Active Matter - (Physiker/in)
jobs.description: In the Department of Living Matter Physics (LMP) we seek to fill a number ofPostdoctoral Researcher positions.- Statistical Physics and Active Matter -The Max Planck Institute for Dynamics and Self-Organization (MPI-DS) at Göttingen, Germany, is an international, interdisciplinary and collaborative environment offering an exceptional research setting. It hosts a range of theoretical and experimental fundamental scientific research and a diverse group of researchers. Altogether, it employs about 300 people. The LMP department engages in a wide range of theoretical research aimed at understanding the dynamics of living systems from a physical perspective. The department currently hosts Ramin Golestanian (director), Philip Bittihn (group leader), Suropriya Saha (group leader), and a number of postdoctoral researchers, students, and visitors.The researchThe postdoctoral researchers will engage in theoretical and computational research in Nonequilibrium Statistical Physics and Active Matter. For more information, visit our website (http://www.ds.mpg.de/lmp (http://www.ds.mpg.de/lmp) ).Your profileWe are looking for excellent, enthusiastic and self-motivated researchers with relevant background and good communication skills to join our research team. The ideal candidate should have:- A PhD/DPhil degree (or comparable) with a background in theoretical physics, applied mathematics or related disciplines from a recognized university;- Prior experience with nonequilibrium statistical physics and a strong interest in active matter physics;- Ability and desire to work in an international team on inter-disciplinary research topics;- Good command of English, which is the working language of the department. German is an asset but not required.Our offerWe are offering excellent working conditions in a highly interdisciplinary and stimulating research environment. Salary is in accordance with the German state public service salary scale (E13 TVöD-Bund) and the corresponding social benefits. Working hours are full time. We offer opportunities regarding work life balance as well as health promotion services. The postdoctoral appointment is for two years. The starting date is flexible.The Max-Planck Society is committed to achieving the highest level of excellence and diversity. We encourage applications from women, especially in areas where they are underrepresented, which includes theoretical physics. Moreover, we are committed to providing suitable working environment for everyone including individuals with disabilities.Your applicationTo apply, please follow this link (https://s.b-ite.com/vd1cg)  and submit your CV, publication list, a statement of research interest, and contacts of two referees. In addition to the description of your proposed research, it should also briefly describe your past and current research interests and why you are interested in joining our department. Processing of applications will start after the deadline of 10th January 2027, and will stop when the positions are filled.  For questions, please contact:Prof. Dr. Ramin Golestanian Tel. +49 551 5176-100Email: golestanian-office@ds.mpg.de (https://mailto:golestanian-office@ds.mpg.de)  Max Planck Institute forDynamics and Self-OrganizationProf. Dr. Ramin GolestanianAm Faßberg 1737077 GöttingenGermany

jobs.occupation: W2 Professorship “Sustainable Freight Transport Systems and Transport Logistics" (Ingenieur/in - Verkehrswesen)
jobs.description: W2 Professorship “Sustainable Freight Transport Systems and Transport Logistics"Application deadline:30.12.2026Date of hire:as soon as possibleVacancy number:39565We are seeking an academically outstanding individual (m/f/d) who will make an independent inter- and transdisciplinary contribution to research in the field of sustainable freight transport systems and logistics. The content focus is at the intersection of value chains, freight transport, and sustainable production systems. The professorship shall connect and strengthen the sustainability-related systems analytical topics at the Kassel Institute for Sustainability and the transportation science topics in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering. Moreover, there is an aim to foster networking in the fields of supply chains and intralogistics with the relevant departments of Economics and Mechanical Engineering. This is intended to further the interdisciplinary interaction between technical and societal research approaches and to advance the research focus on sustainable transformation at the University of Kassel.The professorship should focus on at least one of the following topics:1. Systemic analysis of the interdependencies between freight transport systems, trade, and economic development: Origin of freight transport, economic and ecological evaluation of interregional division of labor, interactions between infrastructure (e.g., rail), regional production clusters and division of labor, as well as sustainable design of these relationships.2. Modeling of the freight transport system: Development and application of scenarios and models for the origin, development, and management of freight transport, infrastructure development and the associated policy instruments, as well as the advancement of corresponding methods.3. Development and application of comprehensive approaches for sustainability evaluation of the ecological, social, and economic effects of strategies and interventions in freight transport, as well as, based on these, the design of a sustainable freight transport system.Experience in the collection, analysis, and management of data in the context of the transformation towards a sustainable freight transport system is also desirable, including the consideration of AI methods: development of data collection procedures and methods of data analysis and data-driven forecasts based on statistical and AI methods, issues regarding the (public) availability and use of data.In teaching, the professorship should supplement and enhance existing degree programs in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, and to develop new or emerging study programs with a focus on sustainability. Teaching responsibilities are to be divided, with 50% in sustainability-related degree programs and 50% in offerings within the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering. Some courses must be taught in English. It is expected that the appointee, especially regarding official duties in teaching and academic self-administration, will acquire sufficient proficiency in the German language in due course, if not already possessed.The main location for the professorship will be at the Kassel Institute for Sustainability.Special notes: The department aims to increase the proportion of female professors and expressly encourages female scientists to apply.The requirements for appointment and performance are in accordance with §§ 67, 68 HessHG. Specifically, a completed, qualified doctorate as well as a habilitation or equivalent additional academic achievements, as evidenced by scientific publications, are required. You should also possess pedagogical aptitude and commitment to academic teaching, as well as a pronounced willingness for interdisciplinary collaboration.Please submit a curriculum vitae, certificates, diplomas, a list of scientific works, three selected publications, a research and teaching concept (maximum three pages each), as well as a list of previous courses taught, existing teaching evaluations, and any higher education didactic trainings with your application. Additionally, please submit a brief concept (maximum three pages) outlining your ideas for a professional and institutional connection to the Kassel Institute for Sustainability.For questions, please contact Prof. Dr. Angela Francke, Tel.: +49 561 804-7703, Email: angela.francke(at)uni-kassel.de. We kindly ask you to submit the complete application documents as a single PDF document via the University of Kassel's application portal.
